subject: Dedicated capacity allocation slate — options for Novaplace
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity allocation slate — options for Novaplace

Katy, Marco —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is a short slate of dedicated capacity options tailored to the traffic profile you shared (sample attached). The intent here is to present 3 distinct allocation bands so your engineering team can map features to cost and activation timelines quickly:

- Band A — Entry floor: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA L40s equiv)
  - Recommended when starting with low-concurrency features and relying on aggressive prefix caching.
  - Activation window: 2–4 weeks.
  - Autoscale: burst to 12 GPUs for sustained 2-minute windows.

- Band B — Production baseline: 32 GPUs
  - Good for mid-stage launch supporting 5–10 RPS steady state for long sequences.
  - Activation window: phased over 6 weeks (8 -> 16 -> 32) with canary at 16.
  - Autoscale: burst to 40 GPUs with priority routing to reduce tail latency.

- Band C — High-availability runway: 96 GPUs
  - Designed for enterprise SLOs, multi-region failover, and heavy batching for cost efficiency.
  - Activation window: 10–12 weeks with adjustable ramp tranches (32 / 64 / 96).
  - Reserve minimum of 64 GPUs for SLAs; remaining 32 can be scheduled as optional buffer.

A few operational notes included in the PDF: minimum GPU floors for SLA, suggested warmup cadence, recommended quantization profile for your model family, and a short runbook for staged activation (rollout steps and rollback triggers).

Next steps I propose: pick the band you want to start with and we’ll produce a granular week-by-week activation plan (including a warmup schedule and load tests). Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the PDF.

Attachments: Novaplace_Redwood_Dedicated_Options_20280809.pdf (pdf), novaplace-usage-sample.csv (csv)

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0123
From: Katy Lin <katy.lin@novaplace.com>

Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco@novaplace.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity allocation slate — options for Novaplace

Tessa —

Thanks, this is a great starting point. A couple quick clarifying questions before we schedule a call: 

1) For Band B you recommend a phased 8 -> 16 -> 32 over six weeks — is that driven by model warmup/CDN population concerns or hardware procurement availability on your side?

2) For Band C you list 96 GPUs with a 64-GPU SLA floor — can we instead structure that as a 48 guaranteed + 48 optional burst to lower our committed minimum?

3) Is multi-region failover (automatic traffic shift) included in your standard Dedicated package or is that an add-on?

Also — attached our current traffic export for the past 30 days; it shows several large bursts that happen during business hours and a steady long-tail overnight. If you can pencil in a cost estimate for steady-state vs burst we can compare to the infra budget.

-Katy
Katy Lin
Head of Platform
Novaplace
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Katy Lin <katy.lin@novaplace.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-10T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity allocation slate — options for Novaplace

Katy —

Thanks for the clear questions. Quick answers and clarifications below.

1) Band B phasing rationale: primarily warmup and cache population. We recommend accelerating in small tranches so KV caches and prefix caches reach effective hit rates before you scale to full footprint. Hardware availability is not a gating factor for us — we maintain capacity across our Dedicated region.

2) Flexible floor for Band C: yes, we can structure as a hybrid commitment (48 guaranteed + 48 on-call burst). Two notes:
  - Pricing delta: hybrid floor reduces monthly committed spend but increases per-burst unit price and reduces guaranteed throughput SLAs on the optional tranche.
  - Operationally: optional tranche is pre-warmed on scheduled windows; for unexpected spikes we rely on graceful degradation + routing fallbacks.

3) Multi-region failover: included for enterprise Dedicated when configured (we treat it as part of the SLA bundle). There is an additional data-transfer and replication configuration cost — we can show both options in the final quote.

Suggested next step: Tessa, Monica and I can produce a 6-week activation calendar for Band B and a hybrid Band C term sheet (48+48). I’ll include expected tail-latency numbers and cost buckets for steady vs burst.
